windowsPreview.title: Windows is a preview
windowsPreview.description: The Windows agent backs files up from a shadow copy (VSS) and restores them. In this release it is a preview: x64 only (no Windows on ARM), restow-agent.exe and restic.exe carry no Authenticode signature (Microsoft Defender, Smart App Control or ASR rules may block them), and there is no restore of the whole machine. script.heading: What the script does

download.linux: Downloads restow-agent and restic from this server, not from the internet.
download.darwin: Downloads restow-agent and restic from this server, not from the internet.
download.windows: Downloads restow-agent.exe and restic.exe from this server, not from the internet.

verify.linux: Checks the maintainer's signature over the release and the SHA-256 checksum of both programs before it runs anything.
verify.darwin: Checks the maintainer's signature over the release and the SHA-256 checksum of both programs before it runs anything.
verify.windows: Checks the maintainer's signature over the release with its own Ed25519 check written in PowerShell, and the SHA-256 checksum of both programs, before it runs anything.

service.linux: Installs both into /opt/restow-agent, a folder only root can change, and registers the agent as a system service (systemd unit restow-agent).

service.windows: Installs both into C:\Program Files\Restow\bin, a folder only SYSTEM and administrators can change, and registers the Windows service RestowAgent (LocalSystem).

files.title: What is backed up
files.description: Folders the agent backs up and patterns it leaves out.

paths.label: Folders to back up
paths.hint: Absolute paths on the machine, for example /home or /srv. Everything below a folder is included.

excludes.label: Exclude patterns
excludes.hint: One pattern per line, for example *.tmp or node_modules. Files that match are left out of the backup.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: When the agent starts a backup.
schedule.noJobDescription: The backup job the machine is in sets the schedule.

minutesHint.on_connect: A backup starts when the machine is online and the last one is older than this. Empty: the agent default of {default} minutes (4 hours).

schedule.timeZoneHint: The time zone the schedule is read in.
schedule.defaults: By default, servers are backed up daily at 22:00 and clients whenever they are online, at most once every 4 hours.

limits.title: Limits
limits.description: Keep backups from disturbing the machine or its network.
limits.bandwidthHint: Empty means unlimited. 1000 kbit/s is about 1 Mbit/s. It applies outside every time window.
limits.acPower: Only back up on AC power
limits.acPowerHint: A laptop on battery skips the backup until it is plugged in.
limits.vssHint: Backs up from a shadow copy, so open and locked files can be read and all files are from the same moment (file consistent). What happens when it fails is set by the agent policy (back up without the snapshot, or stop).

hooks.title: Commands before and after the backup
hooks.description: Commands the agent runs around each backup, for example to dump a database so that its files are consistent. They run as root, so the machine decides whether it runs them.
hooks.warningTitle: These commands run with full rights
hooks.warningRoot: The agent runs them as root (administrator) on the machine, before and after every backup. Only enter commands you trust and understand.
hooks.warningFailure: If the command before the backup fails, the backup fails too, so a broken dump never gets backed up as if it were fine.
hooks.warningAudit: The audit log records that hooks changed and a fingerprint of them, not their text.
hooks.stepUp: Setting or changing a hook asks you to confirm it is you when you signed in more than 10 minutes ago. Removing all hooks does not.
hooks.preHint: Runs first. Leave empty for none.
hooks.postHint: Runs when the backup is over. Leave empty for none.

unknown.title: The machine has not said whether it allows hooks
unknown.description: The agent reports it with its next contact. Until then no hooks can be set here.

off.title: Hooks are switched off on this machine
off.description: Hooks run as root, so only an administrator of the machine can allow them, on the machine itself. It takes one of these commands there:

scripts.title: This machine only runs its own scripts
scripts.description: Enter the name of a script that an administrator put into /etc/restow-agent/hooks.d on the machine, not a command. The agent runs it directly, without a shell.
scripts.none: There are no scripts in /etc/restow-agent/hooks.d on the machine yet.

any.title: This machine runs any command from {appName}
any.description: An administrator of the machine allowed hooks of any kind. Whoever may change this machine's settings in {appName} can run commands as root on it.

hooks.scriptHint: The name of a script in /etc/restow-agent/hooks.d. Leave empty for none.

hidden.set: A command is set (fingerprint {fingerprint}). Only administrators who may change the settings see it.

ignored.title: The commands below are not run
ignored.description: They were set before the machine decided about hooks. The machine skips them and marks each backup as incomplete until they are removed or allowed on the machine.

retention.title: Retention
retention.note: The server applies these rules and removes older snapshots; the agent can only add backups, never delete them. Lowering a number permanently removes older snapshots at the next retention run.

stricter.title: Shorten the retention?
stricter.description: The next retention run removes older restore points of this machine for good, up to:
stricter.keepDaily: {count, plural, one {# daily restore point} other {# daily restore points}}
stricter.keepWeekly: {count, plural, one {# weekly restore point} other {# weekly restore points}}
stricter.keepMonthly: {count, plural, one {# monthly restore point} other {# monthly restore points}}

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.description: When {appName} tells you that this machine needs attention.
alerts.hoursHint: Alert when the server has not been in contact for longer than this. Default: {count}.
alerts.daysHint: Alert when the client has had no successful backup for longer than this. Default: {count}.
alerts.revokeHint: Days without contact before suggesting to revoke
alerts.revokeHintHint: After this many days without contact, the machine suggests revoking it, here and in the list of what needs attention. Default: {count}.

errors.noPaths: Add at least one folder to back up.
errors.timeOfDay: Enter a time as HH:MM, for example 22:00.
errors.notScriptName: Enter the name of a script (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore), not a command.

save.fix: Fix the marked fields before saving.

toast.appliedLater: The machine applies them with its next contact.

quota.title: Storage budget
quota.description: The most the backup data of this machine may take in the repository. Uploads beyond it are refused; restores keep working.
quota.label: Budget in GiB
quota.hintDefault: Leave empty for the installation's default of {size}.
quota.hintUnlimited: Leave empty for no limit (the installation sets none).
quota.tenantNote: All servers and clients of this tenant share a budget of {size}.

fsSnapshot.label: File system snapshot (LVM, btrfs)
fsSnapshot.hint: Backs up from an LVM or btrfs snapshot, so all files are from the same moment (file consistent). File systems without a snapshot method (a partition, a full volume group) are read live. What happens when a snapshot fails is set by the agent policy.

defaultNote.auto: Default for this machine: on, because its job backs it up as a whole.
defaultNote.off: Default for this machine: off. Whole machine backups take snapshots by default.

repositoryKey.title: Restore without {appName}
repositoryKey.description: The backup of this machine is a normal restic repository.
repositoryKey.body: With the repository password and access to the folder or bucket of your repository, you can restore the backup with restic alone, even if this {appName} server is gone. The server also keeps the password sealed next to the restic repository, so the master key and the storage are enough: the command restow-restore endpoint-password recovers it. Keep the password safe all the same, for example in a password manager.

dialog.title: Repository password
dialog.description: Confirm that you want to see the repository password of this machine.
dialog.shownDescription: Copy the password now. It is hidden again when you close this window.
dialog.audit: Showing the password is recorded in the audit log.
dialog.power: The password decrypts the whole backup of this machine. Anyone who has it and can read the repository can read every backed-up file.
dialog.stepUp: If you signed in more than 10 minutes ago, you confirm it is you first.
dialog.hideNote: Not stored in this browser. Closing the window hides it.
dialog.exampleNote: Replace /path/to/storage with the folder of your repository and run restic with this password. It restores the newest snapshot into /restore. For object storage, use the restic repository address of your bucket instead.

danger.title: Stop backing up this machine
danger.description: Uninstalling and revoking delete nothing: the machine stays in the inventory as revoked (hidden until you show revoked machines), and its backups stay restorable. Only removing a revoked machine deletes its backups, when they expire or seven days after the request.

uninstall.title: Uninstall the agent
uninstall.description: The machine removes the agent by itself with its next contact, and is revoked when it does. Use this when you no longer want to back the machine up.
uninstall.queued: The uninstall is waiting for the machine.

confirm.title: Uninstall the agent on {name}?
confirm.description: The agent removes itself from the machine with its next contact. Afterwards the machine is revoked and no longer backed up. Backups that exist stay restorable.
confirm.offline: If the machine is off or offline, this waits until it reports back. To stop it right now, revoke it instead.

toast.already: An uninstall is already waiting for this machine.

uninstall.revokeNowHint: If the machine is off or gone, the uninstall waits for ever. Revoke it now instead; remove the agent on the machine later if it comes back.

revoke.title: Revoke
revoke.description: Refuses the machine at once: no more backups and no more tasks. The agent stays installed on the machine until you remove it there.

confirm.title: Revoke {name}?
confirm.description: From now on the machine is refused: it is no longer backed up and takes no tasks. The agent stays installed and keeps trying until you uninstall it on the machine. Backups that exist stay restorable.
confirm.irreversible: This cannot be undone. To back the machine up again, enroll it anew.

danger.revokeSuggested: {days, plural, one {This machine has not been in contact for more than # day. If it is gone for good, revoke it, then remove it.} other {This machine has not been in contact for more than # days. If it is gone for good, revoke it, then remove it.}}

remove.title: Remove from {appName}
remove.description: Takes the machine out of every list and deletes its backups when its retention lets them go. An owner of the provider team can instead have every backup deleted seven days after the request. Its runs and the audit log keep their entries.
remove.revokeFirst: Revoke the machine first. A machine that is not revoked cannot be removed.

expire.label: Remove from the list, keep the backups until they expire
expire.description: The backups stay stored until the machine's retention would have let the newest of them go, then they are deleted. Until then the page of the removed machine still offers their restore.

delete.label: Delete every backup in seven days
delete.description: The machine stays listed as revoked for seven more days, then every backup of it is deleted and the machine leaves the lists. Until then the deletion can be cancelled. The provider's mandatory recipients are alerted at once. Not possible while a legal hold or an unresolved suspicious restore point holds the backups.
delete.ownerOnly: Only an owner of the provider team can delete backups.

confirm.title: Remove {name}?
confirm.description: This cannot be undone once the deletion has run: deleted backups cannot be restored.
confirm.locks: Backup files the storage still locks (immutable backups) are deleted once their lock runs out; the machines page shows when.

toast.delete: The backups of {name} will be deleted on {date}. You can cancel that on the machine's page until then.
toast.expire: {name} was removed. Its backups are deleted on {date}.

remove.scheduled: The backups of this machine are scheduled for deletion; the notice at the top of the page says when. Cancel that to choose differently.

backupDeletion.title: Backups will be deleted on {date}
backupDeletion.heldLegal: A legal hold over this tenant holds the deletion: nothing is deleted while it stands, and it is checked again daily.
backupDeletion.heldSuspicion: An unresolved suspicious restore point of this machine holds the deletion: nothing is deleted until it is resolved, and it is checked again daily.
backupDeletion.cancelled: The deletion was cancelled. The backups stay.
backupDeletion.ownerCancels: Only an owner of the provider team can cancel the deletion.

errors.resticBusy: The server is reading other backups right now. Try again in a moment.
errors.repositoryLocked: The backup data is busy with a backup or maintenance. Try again shortly.
errors.repositoryUnavailable: The backup data of this machine could not be opened in the repository. Check that the repository is reachable.
errors.repositoryNotFound: The backup data of this machine was not found on any storage target. Check that every storage target of this tenant is reachable and that the machine's folder under endpoints/ was not moved or deleted there.
errors.repositoryPasswordRejected: The stored password does not open the backup data of this machine: the repository was probably re-created or its keys were changed outside {appName}. Contact your provider; the details are in the server log.
errors.repositoryPasswordMissing: No repository password is stored for this machine, so its backup data cannot be opened here. If you saved the password earlier (“Show repository password”), you can still restore with restic outside {appName}.
errors.resticFailed: Reading the backup data failed. The details are in the server log.
errors.resticUnavailable: The restic program is not available on the server, so snapshots cannot be read.
errors.unsupportedOs: This operating system is not supported. {appName} backs up Linux, macOS and Windows on x64 (amd64); Windows on ARM is not supported in this release.
errors.revoked: This machine is revoked and takes no changes or tasks.
errors.noSamples: The newest backup recorded no sample files, so no restore check of it is possible. The run log of the backup says why.
errors.nothingToTest: There is no successful backup to test yet.
errors.instanceUnknown: The address of this installation is not known. Set the public URL in the settings and try again.
errors.queueNotReady: The worker has not started yet. Try again in a moment.
errors.pathNotFound: A selected path is not part of this snapshot.
errors.tokenSettled: This install command was already used or revoked.
errors.downloadGone: This download is no longer available. Prepare it again.
errors.downloadTooLarge: The selection is too large for one download. Select fewer items, or a parent folder.
errors.invalidCursor: The folder listing is out of date. Open the folder again.
errors.hooksNotAllowed: This machine does not allow hooks from {appName}. An administrator of the machine can allow them there with sudo restow-agent hooks scripts or sudo restow-agent hooks any.
errors.hookNotAScript: This machine only runs scripts from /etc/restow-agent/hooks.d. Enter the name of a script there, not a command.
errors.configManagedByJob: This machine is in a backup job, which owns its configuration. Change the schedule, folders, exclusions, commands and bandwidth limit in the job.
errors.noJob: This machine is in no backup job, so it is not backed up. Add it to a job first.
errors.recentSignIn: Confirm it is you first: setting or changing a hook and showing the repository password need a sign-in from the last 10 minutes.
errors.invalidBandwidthWindows: The time windows cannot be saved like this. Check the days, the times and that no two windows overlap.
errors.assigneeUnknown: The person is not in the directory of this tenant (any more). Choose a person from the list.
errors.containerNotBrowsable: This restore point cannot be browsed file by file.
errors.containerNoRepository: The backups of this container are not available on the server.
errors.vmFilesUnreadable: The file system of this restore point could not be read on the server. Restore the whole VM under VMs & containers.
errors.agentPolicyInvalid: A setting of the policy cannot be saved like this. Check the values.
errors.agentPolicyLocked: The installation locked this setting of the policy; it cannot be changed here.
errors.notRevoked: Only a revoked machine can be removed. Revoke it first.
errors.confirmHostname: The hostname does not match. Type it exactly as shown.
errors.removalLegalHold: A legal hold covers every backup of this tenant, so they cannot be deleted now. Keep them until they expire instead, or release the hold first.
errors.removalSuspicionHold: A suspicious restore point of this machine is not resolved and holds its backups. Resolve it first, or keep the backups until they expire.
errors.removalNeverExpires: The retention of this machine keeps every backup, so they would never expire. Delete them instead.
errors.restorePathLocked: This file is not handed out: the agent's own state file is never restored (the agent gets a new identity when it is enrolled again), and key files of encrypted volumes only to administrators.
errors.recoveryCodeInvalid: No recovery code matches. Check the code and the address.
errors.recoveryCodeExpired: The recovery code has expired. Issue a new one.
errors.recoveryCodeRevoked: The recovery code was revoked. Issue a new one.
errors.recoveryCodeUsed: The recovery code was redeemed already. Issue a new one.
errors.recoveryTooOld: The recovery ISO is too old for this server. Download the current one.
errors.recoveryNotApproved: The session has not been released yet.
errors.recoveryCredentialsCollected: The ISO collected the credentials already.
errors.recoveryStateConflict: That is not possible in the current state of the recovery. Reload the page.
errors.baremetalNotAvailable: No recovery code can be issued for this machine.
errors.recoveryLimitReached: Three codes of this machine are open already. Revoke one first.
errors.endpointRecoveryActive: A recovery reads this machine's backups. Let it finish or end it first.
errors.rebindOsMismatch: The token is for a machine with another operating system.
errors.sqlUnsupported: The agent on this machine cannot back up SQL Server natively yet. Update the agent first.
errors.sqlBackupPruned: This backup is no longer kept: retention removed it. Choose a newer one.
errors.sqlNameTaken: A database of that name already exists on the instance. Choose another name.
errors.sqlNothingToVerify: No database of this machine has a backup in the backup data yet.
errors.removalScheduled: The backups of this machine are already scheduled for deletion. Cancel that first to choose differently.
errors.removalReasonRequired: Give a reason for deleting the backups.
errors.removalNotCancellable: The deletion can no longer be cancelled: it has started, or there is none to cancel.
errors.ownerRequired: Only an owner of the provider team can do this.

result.green: The restore check of the newest backup matched every checked file.
result.yellow: The restore check passed, but the newest backup has warnings: some files could not be read.
result.red: The restore check of the newest backup failed, or an integrity check found damage.
result.noSamples: No sample files recorded; restore check not possible for this backup.
result.unverified: A backup exists but was never checked.
result.noBackup: Nothing to verify until the first backup completes.
result.noBackupOverdue: No backup within 24 hours of protection starting.

runErrors.no_paths: None of the configured folders exists on the machine
runErrors.pre_hook_failed: The command before the backup failed, so the backup did not run
runErrors.post_hook_failed: The command after the backup failed
runErrors.hooks_not_allowed: The command before or after the backup was not run: the machine does not allow hooks from {appName}
runErrors.timeout: The run took too long and was stopped
runErrors.target_not_empty: The target folder was not empty, so nothing was restored and nothing was overwritten
runErrors.target_unusable: The target folder could not be used, for example because the folder above it is missing or permissions are lacking. Nothing was restored.
runErrors.invalid_task: The machine could not carry out the request
runErrors.hash_mismatch: A file differs from the checksum recorded at backup time
runErrors.missing: A file was not found in the restore point
runErrors.not_regular: The entry is not a regular file, so it could not be compared
runErrors.read_error: A file could not be read
runErrors.truncated: Further errors are not listed here
runErrors.agent_stopped: The agent stopped reporting while the run was in progress
runErrors.snapshot_failed: The file system snapshot (such as a shadow copy or an LVM or btrfs snapshot) of a drive or file system failed
runErrors.snapshot_unavailable: Without a file system snapshot: snapshots cannot be used on the machine
runErrors.snapshot_cleanup_failed: A file system snapshot was left behind after the backup
runErrors.source_unreadable: A backup folder could not be read, for example a drive locked by BitLocker, offline or without access, and is missing from this backup
runErrors.source_is_mount_point: A backup folder is a volume without a drive letter: only its mount point would be backed up, so it is missing from this backup
runErrors.layout_capture_failed: The disk layout could not be recorded; the mounted file systems were backed up anyway
runErrors.layout_too_large: The disk layout is too large for the server; it is in the restore point, but not shown here
runErrors.layout_rejected: The server did not keep the disk layout the agent sent

agentUpdates.title: Automatic agent updates
agentUpdates.description: Agents update themselves to the newest version this installation ships, and only to releases signed by the maintainer. Pause it to keep every machine on its version, for example to test an update first. It is one setting for all machines, also for machines added later.
agentUpdates.label: Update agents automatically
agentUpdates.on: On: the machines install new signed agent releases by themselves.
agentUpdates.paused: Paused for every machine, also for machines added later.

toast.machineResumed: The machine follows the setting again
toast.allResumed: All machines follow the setting again

agentUpdates.loadError: The setting for agent updates could not be loaded.

overrides.title: {count, plural, one {# machine is paused on its own} other {# machines are paused on their own}}
overrides.description: These machines keep their version whatever the setting above says. They were paused before the pause became one setting for all machines. Resume them to let them follow the setting.

inventory.title: Inventory
inventory.subtitle: Every machine with a backup agent: connection, agent version and recovery readiness.

fileRestore.title: File restore
fileRestore.subtitle: Restore or download files from a restore point of a server, client, or Proxmox VE VM or container. Mailboxes, OneDrives and IMAP accounts are restored in the restore explorer.
fileRestore.noTenant: Choose a tenant at the top to restore files of its machines.

pick.title: Choose a machine
pick.description: Choose a machine on the left. Then choose a restore point on the timeline and restore files.

empty.title: Nothing backed up yet
empty.description: Add a server or client in the inventory. Once it is backed up, restore its files here.
empty.descriptionRestorer: Once a server, client or Proxmox VE guest of this tenant is backed up, you can restore its files here.

fileRestore.noMatchWithContainers: No machine, VM or container matches the search.

pickWithContainers.title: Choose a machine, VM or container
pickWithContainers.description: Choose a machine, VM or container on the left. Then choose a restore point on the timeline and restore or download files.

containerFiles.loadError: The container could not be loaded
containerFiles.notFoundDescription: The container does not exist (any more) in this tenant.
containerFiles.emptyDescription: Once the container is backed up, its files can be browsed and downloaded here.
containerFiles.downloadOnly: Files of a container are downloaded as a ZIP. To put the whole container back, restore it under VMs & containers.
containerFiles.downloadOnlyRestorer: Files of a container are downloaded as a ZIP. Putting the whole container back is up to an administrator.
containerFiles.restoreWholeHint: Puts the whole container back from this restore point (on the container's page).

vmFiles.loadError: The VM could not be loaded
vmFiles.notFoundDescription: The VM does not exist (any more) in this tenant.
vmFiles.emptyDescription: Once the VM is backed up, the files on its disks can be browsed and downloaded here.
vmFiles.downloadOnly: The files of a VM are read from the disks of the restore point on the server, in an isolated reader: nothing is mounted, the VM and its node are not touched. Readable: ext2/3/4, XFS, NTFS and FAT, also on LVM. Files are downloaded as a ZIP; to put the whole VM back, restore it under VMs & containers.
vmFiles.downloadOnlyRestorer: The files of a VM are read from the disks of the restore point on the server, in an isolated reader: nothing is mounted, the VM and its node are not touched. Readable: ext2/3/4, XFS, NTFS and FAT, also on LVM. Files are downloaded as a ZIP; putting the whole VM back is up to an administrator.
vmFiles.restoreWholeHint: Puts the whole VM back from this restore point (on the VM's page).
vmFiles.unreadable: Not readable on this restore point:
vmFiles.volumes: Each folder at the top is a file system of the VM's disks (scsi0-p2: disk scsi0, partition 2; vg0-root: logical volume root of the volume group vg0).
vmFiles.preview: Preview: reading files from VM disks is new. Before you rely on a restored file, compare an important one with the original.

policy.lockedNote: The installation locked this setting: no tenant and no backup job can change it.
policy.lock: Lock for every tenant and backup job

own.global: Set for the installation (otherwise the default applies)
own.tenant: Set for this tenant (otherwise the installation's value applies)
own.job: Set for this job (otherwise the tenant's value applies)

backupWindow.title: Backup window
backupWindow.description: When scheduled backups may start, including catch-ups and retries. A backup that is still running when the window ends continues. Back up now ignores the window.
backupWindow.zone: Times in {zone}, the time zone of the job's schedule.
backupWindow.zoneOfSchedule: Times in the time zone of each machine's schedule.
backupWindow.rules: An end that is not after the start is on the next day; the same time twice is the whole day. Daylight saving time follows the wall clock.

catchUp.title: Catch up missed backups
catchUp.description: A backup is missed when the machine was off or asleep when it was due. A backup that waited while the machine was on (server not reachable, an update of {appName}) is never missed: it starts as soon as it can.
catchUp.off: Off: wait for the next regular backup

modes.asap: As soon as the machine is on again

catchUp.withMaxAge: {mode}, if missed at most {count, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} ago
catchUp.maxAge: Only if missed at most this many hours ago
catchUp.maxAgeHint: Empty: any age. 1 to {max} hours; an older missed backup waits for the next regular one.

bandwidthKbps.title: Upload limit
bandwidthKbps.description: The limit of a backup job that sets none of its own (kbit/s).
bandwidthKbps.label: Upload limit (kbit/s)

onlyOnAcPower.title: Only on AC power
onlyOnAcPower.description: Scheduled backups of laptops wait for the power supply. A machine that is set to this on its own keeps it.

retries.title: Automatic retries
retries.description: How often a failed backup is tried again (after 5, 15 and 30 minutes, then hourly) before the next regular backup.
retries.label: Retries

snapshotOnFailure.title: When the file system snapshot fails
snapshotOnFailure.description: Applies to the shadow copy (VSS) of Windows machines and to file system snapshots on Linux and macOS. A shadow copy makes a backup file consistent, not application consistent; back databases up with a command before the backup as well.

hints.continue: The volumes concerned are read directly; the run ends as partial and says why.
hints.fail: The run ends as failed; the automatic retries apply.

problems.maxAge: Enter whole hours from 1 to 720, or leave it empty.
problems.bandwidth: Enter a whole number of kbit/s, or leave it empty for unlimited.
problems.retries: Enter a whole number from 0 to 10.

policy.loadError: The agent policy could not be loaded.
policy.saved: {count, plural, =0 {Policy saved. No machine needed a new configuration.} one {Policy saved. # machine gets its new configuration.} other {Policy saved. # machines get their new configuration.}}

tenant.title: Agent policy
tenant.description: When and how the agents of this tenant's servers and clients back up. Values you do not set here come from the installation; a backup job can set its own for its machines, unless the installation locked them. Agents from 0.4.0 follow the backup window, catch-up and retries.

global.title: Agent policy
global.description: When and how the agents of servers and clients back up, in every tenant. Tenants and backup jobs can set their own values, except for what you lock here. Without any value set, agents behave as before. Agents from 0.4.0 follow the backup window, catch-up and retries.
global.readOnly: Administrators of the provider with every tenant change the policy; you can read it.

cancel.stopBody: The agent stops restic cleanly with its next contact (within about a minute). Nothing from this run is saved and the repository stays as it was. The run ends as cancelled, not as failed; the next scheduled backup runs as usual.
cancel.withdrawBody: The requested backup has not started yet. It is withdrawn and the machine will not start it.
cancel.stoppingNote: The agent stops it with its next contact, usually within a minute.

agentUpdate.requested: The agent updates as soon as it is idle
agentUpdate.requestedNote: It installs the signed release with its next contact once no backup or restore runs on the machine, then restarts.
agentUpdate.paused: Agent updates are paused for this machine or its tenant.

removals.title: {count, plural, one {Backups of # removed machine} other {Backups of # removed machines}}
removals.description: These machines were removed from {appName}. Their backups are still stored until they are deleted.
removals.deferred: Partly locked by the storage until {date}, deleted after that
removals.deferredUnknown: Partly locked by the storage, deleted once the lock runs out

held.legal: Held by a legal hold over the whole tenant
held.suspicion: Held by an unresolved suspicious restore point

removals.detailNote: This machine was removed from {appName}. Until its backups are deleted, they can be browsed and files downloaded as a ZIP; nothing else.

sheet.title: Machine
sheet.notFound: This machine does not exist (any more), or it belongs to another tenant.
sheet.adminOnly: Backing up and stopping is for administrators of backup jobs.

baremetal.title: Bare-metal restore (preview)

states.not_enabled: Not backed up as a whole

notPossible.container: A container is restored with its host.
notPossible.windows: Windows machines are not restored as a whole yet.
notPossible.darwin_later: macOS follows in a later version.
notPossible.agent_too_old: The agent is too old for a whole machine backup (0.5.0 or later needed).
notPossible.unsupported: The layout uses parts the restore cannot create (see below).
notPossible.arm64_later: Bare-metal restores of arm64 machines follow in a later version.

baremetal.unverifiedHint: The newest whole machine backup recorded the layout below. The server checks after every whole machine backup whether it can be restored; until that check has run, nothing here is proof.
baremetal.snapshotHint: {vg} has no free space for snapshots. Leave {size} free (10 % of the volume group), then {appName} backs up {mounts} consistently.

codes.fs_type_unsupported: A file system of a system path has a type the restore cannot create (for example ZFS, bcachefs, F2FS or NTFS)
codes.lvm_type_unsupported: A logical volume uses a cache, writecache or VDO, which the restore cannot create
codes.md_container_unsupported: A RAID array lives in a firmware RAID container
codes.md_journal_unsupported: A RAID array uses a journal or partial parity log
codes.md_reshape_in_progress: A RAID array was being reshaped during the backup

hints.secure_boot_disabled: The boot chain of this machine did not pass the Secure Boot checks of the replacement hardware. It starts only while Secure Boot is switched off in the firmware setup; the recovery did not switch it off.
hints.selinux_autorelabel: SELinux labels every file again at the first start; let it finish.

rebind.title: Reconnect {name}
rebind.dangerDescription: A token that gives this machine a new agent secret, for a reinstalled or restored system. Its backups, settings and history stay.
rebind.warning: This token gives lasting access like an installed agent. Whoever redeems it becomes this machine.
rebind.oldDisconnects: The previous installation of the machine loses its connection.
rebind.revokedHint: The machine is revoked: without the option below, the token is refused.
rebind.unrevokeHint: Choose this only if the machine was revoked by mistake or is trustworthy again; it is noted in the audit log.

purpose.reinstall: For a machine whose system was installed again.
purpose.baremetal: For the machine the recovery ISO restored.

rebind.created: The token was created. It is shown only now and works once.
rebind.commands: Run the install command on the machine; it asks for the token.

windowsFacts.title: Windows
windowsFacts.description: What the agent reads from the system. Facts only, no rating.
windowsFacts.noRoles: None that needs more than a file backup

app_files_not_app_backup.title: The file backup does not bring these applications back
app_files_not_app_backup.body: This machine runs {subjects}. The file backup holds the files of their open databases, but those files are not a backup these applications can be restored from. Back them up with a tool made for them.
app_files_not_app_backup.sqlHint: For SQL Server, switch on the native SQL Server backup in the backup job of this machine (preview).

sql_log_growing.title: A transaction log keeps growing
sql_log_growing.body: {subjects}: the recovery model is FULL, but nothing backed up the transaction log in the last 24 hours, so the log keeps growing. Back the log up with your existing tool, or switch the database to SIMPLE if you need no point-in-time restore.

sql_tde_certificate.title: Back up the TDE certificate elsewhere
sql_tde_certificate.body: {subjects}: the database is encrypted with TDE. Without its certificate and key, no other instance can restore it. The backup does not contain them; keep them safe elsewhere and confirm it on the SQL Server tab.

sql_version_untested.title: SQL Server version not checked
sql_version_untested.body: {subjects}: this version of SQL Server was not checked with the native backup. It runs, but a restore of it has not been tried.

sql.title: SQL Server
sql.intro: The native SQL Server backup makes a copy-only full backup of each database beside your own backups, so your backup chain stays as it is. A weekly check restores the newest backup from the backup data under a check name and runs DBCC CHECKDB on it. Green only after that check passed.
sql.notCapable: The agent on this machine cannot do this yet. Update it to see and use the native backup.
sql.notEnabled: The native backup is off. Switch it on in the backup job of this machine.
sql.loadError: The SQL Server part of this machine could not be loaded.

instances.title: Instances
instances.noInventory: The agent has not read the instances yet.
instances.none: The agent reports no SQL Server instance.
instances.clustered: Failover cluster instance: not supported by the native backup.
instances.strictEncryption: Strict encryption is on: the agent may not be able to connect.
instances.compressionDefault: Backup compression is on by default on this instance; the agent backs up uncompressed anyway, so the backup data stays deduplicated.

signIn.checkQueued: The machine checks the sign-in with its next contact.
signIn.howTo: The agent signs in as {account} with Windows authentication; no password is stored anywhere. Let a database administrator run this once on the instance:
signIn.sysadminHint: The account becomes a member of sysadmin. Simple, and new databases are covered at once.
signIn.minimalHint: dbcreator, VIEW SERVER STATE and, per database, db_backupoperator and db_owner. A database created later needs these lines again.

databases.title: Databases
databases.description: Checked weekly, {day} at {time} in the zone of the backup job.
databases.emptyHint: The databases appear once the agent read the instance.
databases.notSelected: not taken by the backup job
databases.tde: This database is encrypted with TDE. Back up its certificate and key elsewhere, then confirm it here.

verify.queued: The check of {name} waits for the machine.
verify.alreadyQueued: A check of this instance is already waiting.

restore.title: Restore {name} under a new name
restore.description: The agent fetches the backup from the backup data, checks its checksum and restores it next to the existing database, which stays as it is.
restore.noBackup: No backup of this database is kept.
restore.newNameHint: The database is created under this name; an existing one is never replaced.

nameProblem.tooLong: A name can have at most 128 characters.
nameProblem.control: A name cannot contain control characters.
nameProblem.system: A system database cannot be the target.
nameProblem.reserved: This part of the name is reserved for check databases.
nameProblem.same: Choose a name other than that of the existing database.

restore.checkdb: Check the copy with DBCC CHECKDB
restore.checkdbHint: Recommended. Up to the size set in the backup job the check covers everything, above it the physical structure only.
restore.queued: The restore as {name} waits for the machine.

checkdb.clean: DBCC CHECKDB found no error in the copy.
checkdb.errors: DBCC CHECKDB reported errors in the copy.
checkdb.skipped: DBCC CHECKDB did not run on the copy.

codes.sql_instance_unreachable: The instance could not be reached. Is the SQL Server service running?
codes.sql_login_missing: The agent could not sign in: the instance has no login for it.
codes.sql_permission_missing: The agent signed in, but lacks rights for the backup.
codes.sql_powershell_constrained: The script environment of Windows runs restricted (Constrained Language Mode), so the agent cannot connect.
codes.sql_strict_encryption: The instance requires strict encryption; the native backup does not connect to it.
codes.sql_fci_unsupported: Failover cluster instances are not supported by the native backup.
codes.sql_mode_unsupported: The agent does not know the backup mode set in the job. Update the agent.
codes.sql_staging_unusable: The staging folder cannot be used.
codes.sql_staging_too_small: Not enough free space in the staging folder.
codes.sql_backup_failed: SQL Server could not make the backup.
codes.sql_snapshot_failed: The backup file could not be stored in the backup data.
codes.sql_script_failed: The SQL script of the agent ended unexpectedly.
codes.sql_restore_name_taken: A database of that name already exists.
codes.sql_restore_no_space: Not enough free space for the restore.
codes.sql_backup_mismatch: The backup fetched from the backup data differs from the one made.
codes.sql_verify_no_space: Not enough free space for the check: incomplete, not failed.
codes.sql_verify_timeout: The check took too long and was stopped: incomplete, not failed.
codes.sql_verify_system_db: This system database cannot be checked under a new name.
codes.sql_verify_incomplete: The check came to no result.
